text: The one-by-one Gram matrix is [a], so its radical is zero exactly when a≠0. The NeZero premise therefore gives precisely the nondegenerate member of the family ⟨a⟩ in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4), without asserting unimodularity. The excluded zero parameter is degenerate.
Unimodularity requires a unit, a stronger condition than nonzero.

The self-pairing of an integer k is 2mk², which is twice an integer. This is exactly evenness of the rank-one form in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4), including negative m and m=0. The integral self-pairing is exactly ak².
Evenness of the lattice is precisely evenness of its parameter.

The singleton basis gives carrier ℤ⊂ℚ and Gram matrix [a], hence B(x,y)=axy. This is exactly ⟨a⟩ in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). The parameter is a itself, not twice a; a=0 deliberately gives a rank-one degenerate form. The form is axy on arbitrary rational vectors.
The full carrier is exactly the integer image.
Zero parameter has signature (0,1,0).

The norm of k is ak²: even a makes every norm even, while testing k=1 forces a even. This proves both directions of the parity criterion for ⟨a⟩ in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4), including the zero parameter. Integer representatives have norm ak².
All even parameters give even lattices.

The standard basis consists of 1 and the supplied matrix has the single entry c=a. Thus both constructions have the same integer carrier and the same pairing axy, yielding literal lattice equality. This is the rank-one Gram model in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). The resulting ambient pairing is axy.
Its signed determinant is the unique matrix entry a.

The Gram determinant of the standard integral basis is det[a]=a. Basis independence therefore gives the displayed signed integer, agreeing with the Gram convention for ⟨a⟩ in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). Negative and zero parameters retain their signs and degeneracy. The separate nonnegative invariant is |a|.
Zero determinant is genuinely degenerate here.

Negating a lattice keeps its carrier and negates its bilinear form. Applied to parameter −a this produces −(−axy)=axy on the same ℤ⊂ℚ, giving equality for every a. This uses the form-scaling convention in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). The family pairing is axy.
The negative rank-one root model is the member with a=−2.

For a<0, ax² is negative for every nonzero rational x. The rank is one, so the ordered triple of positive, null and negative indices is (0,0,1). This specializes the signature of the form in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4); Lean puts the null index in the middle. The mandatory parameter−2 control has signature (0,0,1).
The same negative root model is negative definite.

For a>0, ax² is positive for every nonzero rational x. A one-dimensional positive definite form has signature (1,0,0) in Lean’s positive/null/negative order, consistent with the form in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L218) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L319) passes.
At the excluded zero boundary the signature changes to (0,1,0).
The negative parameter−2 control puts the nonzero index in the negative slot.

The self-pairing is ax². Since x²>0 for x≠0 and a<0, it is strictly negative, exactly the negative-definite condition for the rank-one form in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). The hypothesis retains the sign needed for the conclusion. Parameter−2 realizes the mandatory negative-definite control.
Its signature is (0,0,1).
The converse recovers a<0 by testing 1.

The self-pairing ax² is strictly positive for every x≠0 when a>0. This is precisely positive definiteness of the rank-one form in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4), with no integrality restriction on the tested rational vector. Testing the vector1 proves the converse sign condition.
The zero parameter has a null direction and is excluded.

The integer span of the singleton rational basis vector1 consists exactly of integer casts. Hence the existential describes the complete carrier of ⟨a⟩ from [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4), independently of the Gram parameter and including a=0. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L86) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L71) passes.
The carrier has integer rank1 for every parameter.
Integer representatives give the expected integral pairing akl.

With singleton Gram matrix [a], the bilinear matrix formula reduces to axy. The equation holds on the whole rational ambient space, while its restriction to integer vectors is the form ⟨a⟩ in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). On carrier representatives k,l the integer value is akl.
Diagonal evaluation gives ax².

The dual quotient is (a⁻¹ℤ)/ℤ≃ℤ/aℤ, so its order is |a|. This is the rank-one case of the absolute Gram-determinant formula in [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). NeZero excludes the infinite degenerate quotient. The cyclic identification sends kg to the residue of k.
The nonnegative determinant invariant is |a|.

The numeric discriminant is defined as the natural absolute value of the signed determinant. Since det[a]=a, it is |a|, agreeing with the nondegenerate group-order formula in [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). The equality itself also allows a=0. The signed determinant remains a.
For a≠0, |a| is the actual discriminant-group order.

The representative k/a has self-pairing k²/a, so its half-norm is k²/(2a) modulo ℤ. Even a makes this independent of changing k by a multiple of a. This is [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7) after dividing its Q/2ℤ-valued self-pairing by two; the nonzero and even premises are explicit. At the generator the value is 1/(2a) modulo ℤ.
The polar normalization gives kl/a modulo ℤ.

The selected class is the image of the actual dual vector1/a under the quotient map a⁻¹ℤ→a⁻¹ℤ/ℤ. This is the canonical generator of the rank-one discriminant group in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7); when |a|=1 it correctly becomes zero. The class corresponds to1 in ZMod |a|.
Its integer multiples generate the whole discriminant group.

Multiplication by a identifies the dual a⁻¹ℤ with ℤ and sends the embedded original lattice to aℤ. Passing to quotients yields the stated additive equivalence with ZMod |a|, realizing the discriminant quotient of [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). Either sign of nonzero a is allowed. The chosen equivalence sends 1/a+ℤ to1.
Its group has |a| elements.

The additive equivalence sends g=1/a+ℤ to1, so it sends kg to k modulo |a| by preservation of integer multiples. This gives the explicit coordinates for the quotient in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7), for negative as well as positive k and a. The generator maps to1.
Multiples are represented by k/a.

The dual generator has ambient value1/a, and integer scalar multiplication in the subtype is inherited from ℚ. Its k-fold multiple therefore has value k/a, the rank-one dual coordinates used in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). The generator has the exact ambient value1/a.
The same formula describes the integral parametrization of the dual.

An integer k maps to k/a in the dual; this lies in the original carrier exactly when a divides k. Thus the inverse image is the principal ideal (a), which supplies the denominator in ℤ/aℤ for the quotient construction of [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). The induced quotient equivalence sends the distinguished generator to1.

The inverse dual parametrization sends1/a to1, and the subsequent quotient map sends1 to its residue class. Consequently the specified discriminant equivalence sends g to1, fixing the generator convention in the quotient of [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). All integer multiples consequently map to their residues.

The linear map k↦k/a is injective because a≠0 and surjective by the integral-pairing description of the dual. Bundling it therefore gives exactly ℤ≃a⁻¹ℤ, the rank-one instance of the dual realization in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). The equivalence evaluates to k/a on every integer.
The original lattice corresponds to aℤ.

The rational vector1/a pairs with every original integer z to give z, so it belongs to the dual. The subtype bundles this vector and that membership proof, exactly the rank-one dual generator supplied by [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). Forgetting the subtype gives1/a.
Every dual vector is an integer multiple of this vector.

The quotient projection is additive and therefore preserves integer scalar multiples. Applying it to the dual generator identifies kg with the class represented by k/a, as required by the discriminant quotient in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). The same class corresponds to the residue k.

The equivalence bundles the linear map sending k to k times the dual generator. Coercing to ℚ gives k(1/a)=k/a, so this equation fixes its exact normalization in the dual realization of [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). The parameter1 gives the distinguished dual generator.

The definition stores precisely the rational vector1/a, so the subtype coercion returns it. This fixes the generator normalization for the ambient dual described in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7); the nonzero premise supports its membership proof. All integer multiples have ambient value k/a.

Pairing x with the lattice vector1 forces ax∈ℤ. Conversely, if x=k/a then pairing with any integer z gives kz∈ℤ. Thus the dual is exactly a⁻¹ℤ, the rank-one specialization of [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7); division uses a≠0. The same dual is the integer span of1/a.
Its integral parametrization is k↦k/a.

The specified linear parametrization sends1 to1 times the dual generator, hence to the generator itself. This identifies the chosen basis of the dual in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7), rather than merely asserting an unspecified rank-one isomorphism. The ambient formula is k/a for arbitrary k.
The generator has ambient value1/a.

Dual membership says the ambient vector equals k/a for some integer k. This is the coercion of k times the selected generator, and subtype injectivity yields the displayed equality. It proves generation of the actual dual in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7), retaining a≠0.
